name: Alpengarten Kitzbühel
kurzbeschreibung: The Alpine Flower Garden on the Kitzbüheler Horn showcases over 300 to 400 rare high-mountain plant species from the Alps and global ranges at 1,880 m – with free admission.
beschreibung:
Overview

The Alpine Flower Garden on the Kitzbüheler Horn is a botanical gem located at an altitude of approximately 1,880 meters, just below the summit of the Kitzbüheler Horn (1,996 m). Spread across roughly 20,000 m² of alpine rock and pasture, it features over 300 to 400 alpine plant species from mountain ranges across the globe, accompanied by a panoramic 360-degree view of the Kitzbühel Alps and Wilder Kaiser.

History & Botany

Established in 1984 and officially opened in 1985, the garden was founded by cable car manager Richard Profanter, local residents Toni and Eva Hofer, and Prof. Herbert Reisigl from the University of Innsbruck. Alongside native Eastern Alps species like edelweiss, gentian, and alpenrose, it nurtures high-altitude flora from the Pyrenees, Andes, Caucasus, and Himalayas. Peak flowering time is between June and August.

Visit & Getting There

Open daily from late May to late October from 08:30 to 17:00 during summer cable car operating hours (closed in winter). Garden admission is free. Access via the Hornbahn cable car or via the panoramic toll road to the Alpenhaus (1,670 m) followed by a 30–45 minute hike.

Tips

Due to steep, natural alpine terrain with narrow gravel paths and rock steps, the garden is not wheelchair-accessible. Sturdy footwear and good footing are required.
